title: 2015 AMC 12A Problem 13
statement: A league with \(12\) teams holds a round-robin tournament, with each team playing every other team exactly once. Games either end with one team victorious or else end in a draw. A team scores \(2\) points for every game it wins and \(1\) point for every game it draws. Which of the following is not a true statement about the list of \(12\) scores?

answerChoices.label: A
answerChoices.text: There must be an even number of odd scores.

answerChoices.label: B
answerChoices.text: There must be an even number of even scores.

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text: There cannot be two scores of \(0.\)

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text: The sum of the scores must be at least \(100.\)

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text: The highest score must be at least \(12.\)

solutions.text:
Each of the \(12\) teams plays \(11\) games, so \(\dfrac{12\cdot 11}{2} = 66\) games are played, and each game adds \(2\) points to the list. The total of all scores is \(66\cdot 2 = 132.\)

If every game is a draw, each team scores \(11,\) so the highest score need not reach \(12;\) thus statement \(\text{(E)}\) can fail. The other statements always hold: the sum \(132 \ge 100,\) the sum being even forces an even number of odd scores and hence an even number of even scores, and two teams cannot both score \(0\) because their mutual game gives at least one of them a point.

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Every game contributes exactly \(2\) points in total, so the sum of all scores is fixed
Consider what happens if every single game ends in a draw
